candidates.source_summary: Police seized six vehicles during a road safety operation in Rochdale yesterday.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Police seized six vehicles during a road safety operation in Rochdale yesterday. The operation involved officers from Rochdale North and Rochdale East neighbourhood policing teams, who worked alongside officers from Greater Manchester Police’s traffic division and Rochdale Council’s Licensing and Trading Standards teams. The teams stopped 104 vehicles and seized six, including an e-scooter. One driver was arrested on suspicion of drug-driving and 11 were reported for having illegal number plates. One driver was reported for not wearing their seat belt and another was reported for driving without a licence. Two motorists were reported for driving without insurance and another for operating a vehicle without an MOT. candidates.source_summary: Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC has teamed up with new fitness centre Gymbound in a special partnership for the 2027 and 2028 seasons.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC has teamed up with new fitness centre Gymbound in a special partnership for the 2027 and 2028 seasons. Gymbound will become the club’s official club-wide main shirt sponsor, with its branding set to feature on the front of playing shirts across every section of the club, from its youngest players through to its senior teams as Rochdale Mayfield prepares to celebrate its historic 70th anniversary in 2028. The agreement will also see Gymbound, in Eagle Technology Park, Queensway, support Rochdale Mayfield’s open-age pre-season training programme, providing players with access to a modern fitness environment to help improve strength, conditioning, fitness and overall preparation ahead of the new season. The partnership will introduce exclusive membership opportunities for Rochdale Mayfield players and club members, encouraging greater participation in physical activity and making fitness more accessible. Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC founder Carl Abraham said: “We are absolutely delighted to welcome Gymbound on board as our club-wide main shirt sponsor for the 2027 and 2028 seasons. “This is a significant partnership for Rochdale Mayfield and another major step forward in our ambition to become the best amateur sports club in the borough. “As a club, we are constantly looking to build relationships with local businesses that share our values, ambitions and commitment to the community. Gymbound is a fantastic example of that. “What makes this partnership particularly exciting is that it goes far beyond simply having a company’s name on our playing shirts. The support Gymbound will provide through our open-age pre-season programme, alongside exclusive membership opportunities for our players and members, demonstrates a genuine commitment to investing in the health, fitness and wellbeing of our club.
candidates.source_title: Rugby club unveils new gym as shirt sponsor - Rochdale Times

Elton councillor Jack Rydeheard has been putting up the displays since 2021. The councillors plan to repeat the activity each year and will take down the poppies shortly after the Remembrance period. Cllr Rydeheard said, “I am immensely proud that every one of our councillors has helped bring the poppy to the streets of their wards this year.” He added, “Seeing poppies on our lampposts is a simple but powerful reminder of that debt. We will continue this tradition every year, expanding it if we can, and I would encourage everyone to support the Royal British Legion and attend their local Remembrance service.” Residents can support veterans and their families by donating to the Royal British Legion at britishlegion.org.uk . candidates.source_summary: Paul Ferry has been appointed chair of Heywood’s Pride in Place board, with Claire Yardley and Nina Burns joining as new board members.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Paul Ferry has been appointed chair of Heywood’s Pride in Place board, with Claire Yardley and Nina Burns joining as new board members. Paul, who was born and raised in Heywood, runs Well Foundation, a charity working locally with young people aged 10 to 25. He previously spent 10 years as chair of governors at Hopwood Community Primary School. The appointments come as the board prepares to develop projects addressing priorities identified through consultation with residents. Paul said these included crime and anti-social behaviour, transport links and young people. He said, “We have a chance to make big improvements for the town, by listening to the community and investing in those things which will make a real difference. We have to work together so that every nook and cranny of the town is the best it can be.” He said residents would be involved in deciding which projects should receive funding. “Now that we have the funding, we can look at specific projects to improve these. We want to listen to everyone who lives here and make them part of that decision-making.” Elsie Blundell, identified in the announcement as Heywood’s MP, said the Government had confirmed funding was now flowing to the scheme.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Doncaster Rovers assistant coach Cliff Byrne praised his side’s ruthless nature in front of goal during their comfortable 4-1 victory away at Rochdale in the EFL Trophy. Rovers started the game in disappointing fashion, falling behind in the 15th minute after Ian Henderson’s opener after a poor error from Sean Grehan, but started to build momentum in the second half of the contest, equalising through Alfie May after some great work from Harry Clifton to assist the goal. Discussing Clifton’s performance, Byrne said: “He's been chomping at the bit really hard to get going, he's had a little bit of a stop-start with the injury that he had. But you're seeing him there this evening. The energy he brings to the team, the opportunity, the creativity. So, I'm sure he'll be pleased to get some strong minutes under his belt.” Clifton’s performance was a real positive from the victory, another was the goal from Brandon Hanlan - his first of the season - after a bit of a dry patch in front of goal in recent months. “All the forward players, they sort of inwardly judge themselves on the numbers, what they score, what they set up. But he does tireless work for the group, for the team. Brandon, from his own recognition,he understands he wants to get in the box more and more. “We say to all the forward players, the more you end up in there,the more opportunity will come your way. I'm really delighted for him tonight to get that one.” Hanlan benefited from an assist from Jordan Thomas, with the winger coming on at half-time to set up two goals and make a real difference in a contest which Rovers needed to win to be sure of their place in the knockout stages. “He's going to be a top, top player,” Byrne said. “ We've tracked Jordan for a number of, probably nearly 12 months, maybe 18 months prior to him coming in. So, we do have to freshen them up and rotate them around at times, even though they don't pretty much like that version of it. But Jordan's come on tonight and I think he's showcased what he's all about and what he's going to be capable of and I think he'll grow and grow.” Byrne went on to praise the impact of fellow substitute Owen Bailey. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A homeowner faces having to tear down a garden fence because of the impact it has on the neighbouring area. Rochdale Council refused Caterina Buonocore’s application for retrospective planning permission for the 1.55m high boundary fence — about twice the height of the original — around 19 Town House Road, Littleborough. She appealed that decision. But yesterday, a Planning Inspector rejected the appeal, stating: “The main issue is the effect of the appeal development on the character and appearance of the area. “Boundary treatments in the area are typically low-level and visually permeable, contributing to a sense of openness and allowing the soft landscaping within front gardens to remain appreciable. The existing greenery helps to soften the street scene and makes a positive contribution to the character and appearance of the area. “The appeal development introduces a close-boarded timber fence. The height, materials and extensive continuous form of enclosure contrasts with the more open and traditional forms of boundary treatment typically found in the locality. “On site, I observed that due to the prominent corner location, when seen from Park View against the back drop of traditional stone terraces with low-key forms of boundary treatment, the appeal development appears particularly stark and incongruous within the street scene. candidates.source_summary: 'Terrific at times' - Cliff Byrne's assessment of Doncaster Rovers' performance against Rochdale Doncaster Free Press
candidates.source_body_excerpt: It was Jersey Mike’s delight for Doncaster Rovers, who came back from behind to secure a thumping 4-1 victory away at Rochdale. There was nine changes made from the team that were hammered by MK Dons on Saturday, with Brandon Hanlan marking his return to the starting lineup with his first goal this season, in an evening which also saw Alfie May, Owen Bailey and Isaac Hutchinson all add to their tallies for the season. Cliff Byrne said: “At the start, we wanted to secure our place in the next round. I think the level of the performance tonight was terrific at times. It was exhilarating. I know we didn’t have many fans in the stadium tonight but the ones that were here I think will appreciate that.” Rovers came from behind to secure the victory, marking the first time the team has managed that across all competitions since beating Rotherham United on derby day back in February. Sean Grehan was at fault for Rochdale’s opener in a challenging evening for the young defender, who was replaced by Owen Bailey at half-time. He added: “We did conceded from an error and our behalf and we got punished for it. I think over the course of the game we had a lot of control and we showed in particular during the second-half a lot of calmness in the top end of the pitch, which resulted in the four goals.” Reflecting on his team’s spirit along with the first-half error, Byrne added: “We ask the players to play a particular way and we give them autonomy within that to be flexible within the guidelines of how we like to play. Sometimes mistakes can happen and it’s important that we don’t be overly critical because we want players to take opportunites and we want them to be risk takers as well. “It’s important that the whole group contribute and I think we’ve seen that tonight.”

candidates.source_summary: 'Played with intent', 'A true captain's performance': Doncaster Rovers player ratings from EFL Trophy win at Rochdale Doncaster Free Press
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Doncaster Rovers came from behind to secure a well-deserved 4-1 victory away at Rochdale, securing their place in the knockout stages of the EFL Trophy in the process. Grant McCann made nine changes from the team that was thrashed away at MK Dons on Saturday. Josh Clarke was selected in goal, Jay McGrath and Tom Nixon returned to the defence while there was also opportunities for the likes of Harry Clifton, Darren Robinson, Bayley McCann and Brandon Hanlan among others. Jack Senior and Sean Grehan were the only players to keep their place in the starting lineup. Doncaster Rovers got off to a challenging start and were forced into an early change after just three minutes when new arrival Will Keane was forced off with an injury. Hanlan could and probably should have put Rovers in the driving seat moments later, but was denied by a strong save by Sam Waller. Matters got worse after 15 minutes when the hosts took an early lead, latching on to a mistake from Sean Grehan, which allowed Ian Henderson to easily tap home from close-range on his record-breaking 532nd appearance for the Dale. McCann’s men made more changes at the break, introducing both Owen Bailey and Jordan Thomas in an effort to rejuvenate their hopes of progressing to the next stage of the competition and it very much worked the trick. Rovers levelled proceedings in the 54th minute through Alfie May’s close distance strike after great work from Clifton in the build-up. The Vikings then the took the lead nine minutes later when Hanlan netted his first of the season from close range after some brilliant work by both McGrath and Thomas. Bailey, who was brought on to play centre-back in the second half, put the game to bed with a close-range finish in the 88th minute, capping off a true captain’s performance from the 27-year-old. Subsitute Isaac Hutchinson then topped off a great day for the visitors with a goal from close distance. Here are our player ratings from Doncaster Rovers’ final EFL Trophy group stage game.

candidates.source_summary: Rochdale council and Hopwood DePree went head to head in a High Court trial in September. But the next steps for the historic hall is are yet to be determined
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Just over a month on from the High Court battle over Hopwood Hall, the door has been left open for reconciliation. Hopwood DePree, an American filmmaker who wanted to buy the historic landmark from Rochdale Council, had entered an option agreement with the council to restore the hall back in 2017, until that agreement was terminated by the council in October 2024. Since then, Mr DePree, who claims ancestral connections with the 1400s stately home, has felt he had a legally binding agreement to purchase Hopwood Hall for £1. However, in September, following a two-day trial in Manchester Civil Justice Centre, the court ruled that the council was not acting unlawfully when it ended the exclusivity agreement with the American filmmaker. To get the very latest from Manchester's political scene in your newsfeed - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source The High Court found that the ‘change of use’ planning approval granted in 2022 wasn’t enough to trigger the option to purchase the hall for a ‘peppercorn fee’ – £1. candidates.source_summary: ‘Go as far as we can - Cliff Byrne looks ahead to Doncaster Rovers’ EFL Trophy clash with Rochdale Doncaster Free Press
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Doncaster Rovers assistant coach Cliff Byrne believes Tuesday night’s EFL Trophy clash with Rochdale gives the players the perfect chance to try and rectify some of the problems that were apparent during last Saturday’s 6-1 defeat to MK Dons. Rovers go into their final group stage game in second position with a record of three points from their opening two matches. Grant McCann’s men were beaten 3-1 by Huddersfield Town in the first game before more recently recording a 1-0 win over Liverpool Under-21s. It means they are firmly on course to reach the knockout stages of the competition provided they can pick up all three points or either equal or better Liverpool Under-21’s result against Huddersfield. Rochdale are currently on one point. They drew 3-3 with Liverpool Under-21s before losing on penalties in the first match before falling to a disappointing 5-0 defeat against Huddersfield. Reflecting on the weekend, Byrne told club media: “It was a game that was important that we looked back over and looked through and it's a game we have to quickly learn from. “So our benefit now is we’ve got a game coming quickly, so we’re looking forward to that and to be able to go and put a performance on, it’s a game we need to win, it’s a cup competition and we want to progress to the next round, so that’s where the focus is.” Byrne continued: “I think when you come off a poor defeat and a poor performance couple with it, you definitely want an opportunity to go and rectify it and put it right, so when you have a game within a couple of days, that gives you the opportunity to go and do that and that’s exactly what we’ll be aiming to do.” Rovers reached the semi-final of this competition and only narrowly missed out on a first visit to Wembley since 2008 after losing to Stockport County in the semi-final. The South Yorkshire side have only ever won this competition once. That came in 2007 when Sean O’Driscoll’s men were triumphant over Bristol Rovers at the Millenium Stadium. “We want to go as far as we can,” said Byrne. “We made no bones about it last season and this season we have had some really good teams in our group, we’re down to the last game and it’s in our hands to progress to the next round.” The EFL Trophy is often seen as a competition for youngsters and squad players to get an opportunity. Byrne hinted that they’ll be some changes but also emphasized the importance of picking up a good result. He said: “It’s a game we want to win and the selection we have in mind is for that, to win the game and progress. “But there may be an opportunity for some players to get more minutes than they have in recent weeks but I think that's the nature of how the schedule is. It’s very hard to ask the same 11 to go time and time again. They’ll be opportunities in some areas but in others there won’t be.”

candidates.source_summary: Planners' refusal of a bid to turn a former care home into university accommodation has been upheld.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: An appeal over plans to turn a former care home into university accommodation has been dismissed. The Al Sadiq Academy appealed to the Planning Inspectorate after Rochdale Council refused permission to change the use of the former Briarmede care home, in Rochdale Road, Middleton, into university accommodation. The plans included creating 11 en-suite bedrooms, with kitchens and dining hall/games room, library, study rooms, computer rooms and toilets on the ground floor. Planning offices recommended approval for the application, which would have included conditions the building is solely for the use of residents and was not used to provide classes, education services or private or community events at any time. But the application was called in by the council’s planning committee which refused it following concerns about the need for the facility, and the impact it would have on neighbours. In delivering the appeal decision, planning inspector K Mee said: “The main issues are whether the appeal site is a suitable location having regard to the local development plan, insofar as it relates to the type of accommodation; and the effect of the proposed development on the character of the surrounding area and the living conditions of neighbouring residents, with regard to noise and disturbance. “The appellant identifies a number of higher education institutions across Greater Manchester, including Hopwood Hall College opposite the appeal site, as potential sources of demand for student accommodation. “However, no substantive evidence has been provided to demonstrate that these institutions have been consulted regarding the proposals, nor that there is an identified unmet need for additional student accommodation either locally or across the wider area.

Rochdale Council has approved Self-Storage Performance Management International Ltd’s planning application to replace the building in Old Hall Street after it was destroyed by fire in June last year. Instead of a like-for-like replacement, SSPMI will now create a £12 million smaller, taller, mixed-use building with self-storage units on the upper floors and commercial units on the ground floor. The new building will occupy half the footprint of the former Storage World units, but will include two extra storeys to deliver the same capacity inside. In documents submitted with the application, P4 Planning said: “The applicant’s key objective following the catastrophic fire is to replace the building with a suitable modern design that will bring back SME business activity and self-storage space as quickly as possible. “Through close engagement with the council planning and other departments, the applicant is keen to deliver a far better development, with a more appropriate design and format that will also bring wider regeneration benefits. “The mix of uses and economic benefits, design and wider potential benefits will all have a positive impact on the future regeneration of Middleton town centre. “The scale, mass and materials draw reference from the historic research and the site’s past, when Albany Mill was present on the site until 1975.”
candidates.source_title: Decision made over rebuilding of Storage World - Rochdale Times

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Actor Mark Winstanley is returning to the stage after a five-year gap following his multiple sclerosis diagnosis, with a performance of Cabaret Schmabaret in Rochdale. The Performers’ Playground will bring the comedy show to the Ukrainian Centre on 19 November. The Manchester-based theatre training and performance company is run by Mark and Alice Robinson and specialises in comic live theatre. Before his diagnosis, Mark performed nationally and internationally with touring companies including A Ship of Fools Theatre Company, Vamos Theatre and A Plague of Idiots. The company is also fundraising for a separate production of Ubu Royale , with rehearsals and performances designed around Mark’s impaired mobility and fatigue. The project is in research and development, with plans to share the work this year before a proposed national tour in 2027. Ubu Royale is Neil Bartlett’s translation of Alfred Jarry’s Ubu Roi . It follows Pa Ubu and Ma Ubu, two would-be monarchs whose pursuit of power leads to chaos. The production will feature three performers playing more than 20 characters, using puppetry and a set built from discarded materials and repurposed mobility aids.

candidates.source_summary: Rochdale has been allocated £2.24 million from a government fund to help bring long-term empty and derelict buildings back into community or commercial use.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale has been allocated £2.24 million from a government fund to help bring long-term empty and derelict buildings back into community or commercial use. The borough is among sixty council areas receiving support through the £125 million Derelict Buildings Fund. The funding can help councils buy neglected buildings, address financial barriers preventing redevelopment and support community groups or businesses taking over properties. Rochdale MP Paul Waugh will act as a programme champion for the fund, according to the announcement from his office. He highlighted the former Kingsway Hotel and Littleborough’s Wheatsheaf as buildings whose futures concern local residents. Neither is confirmed in the supplied announcement as a recipient of funding. The Wheatsheaf, which closed in June, forms part of the Grade II listed Roundhouse building dating from the early 1860s. In October, Rochdale Council passed a motion brought by Littleborough Lakeside councillor Richard Jackson calling for government action against restrictive covenants on pub sales. Such restrictions can prevent a property being used as a pub after it is sold. Mr Waugh has written to ministers supporting the campaign.

candidates.source_summary: A topping out ceremony has marked a stage in the construction of Hopwood Hall College’s Clegg Building in Rochdale.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A topping out ceremony has marked a stage in the construction of Hopwood Hall College’s Clegg Building in Rochdale. The development, being built by Willmott Dixon, is funded by the Department for Education, Rochdale Council and the college and is scheduled to open in late 2027. The building is named after Robert Clegg OBE, who served as chair of the college’s corporation from 2007 to 2018 and died in September 2021. His wife Anne, son Richard and daughter Emma attended the ceremony. Emma is continuing the family’s connection with Hopwood Hall as a part-time adult learner. They joined principal and chief executive Julia Heap OBE, Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, and the Mayor and Mayoress of Rochdale, Faisal Rana and Iram Faisal, among other guests. Willmott Dixon staff led visitors to the roof, which overlooks landmarks including Rochdale Town Hall and St Chad’s Parish Church. Guests were invited to leave messages on part of the roof parapet as a permanent record of the occasion. The college says the building will provide technical learning facilities for students of all ages. School leavers attending its open events have also been given a glimpse of the development.

candidates.source_summary: Springhill Hospice has received £1,500 from David Wilson Homes to help meet its general running costs.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Springhill Hospice has received £1,500 from David Wilson Homes to help meet its general running costs. The donation was made through the Barratt Redrow Foundation, the housebuilding group’s charitable arm. The hospice has provided specialist palliative care since 1989, serving adults and their families across Rochdale, Middleton and Heywood. Its purpose-built facility has 16 beds and provides physical, psychological, emotional and spiritual care without charge. Vicki Barnett, senior corporate fundraiser at Springhill Hospice, said “This vital funding comes at a crucial time as the Hospice continues to navigate rising costs and increasing demand for palliative and end of life care services.” She added “Every donation we receive makes a genuine difference to the families we support, and we are deeply grateful for this generosity. It helps us continue providing compassionate care at the most difficult moments in people’s lives, and knowing our community stands behind us means a lot.” Jennifer Burns, sales director at David Wilson Homes NW, said the company hoped the donation would help the hospice continue its work across Rochdale. candidates.source_summary: Rochdale and Bury recorded the largest increases in driving test pass rates across Greater Manchester in the year to March 2026, according to DVSA figures.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale and Bury recorded the largest increases in driving test pass rates across Greater Manchester in the year to March 2026, according to DVSA figures. Rochdale’s rate rose from 41.2 per cent to 48.3 per cent, while Bury’s increased from 40.3 per cent to 46.3 per cent. The changes represent increases of 7.1 percentage points at Rochdale and six percentage points at Bury compared with the previous financial year. Both centres remained below the Greater Manchester pass rate of 48.5 per cent and the Great Britain figure of 50 per cent. Across Greater Manchester’s nine centres, 52,716 of the 108,750 practical car tests taken between April 2025 and March 2026 resulted in a pass, according to the driving school’s analysis. Bredbury had the highest pass rate at 56 per cent. Bolton and Sale were the only other centres above the national figure, recording 51.8 per cent and 51.4 per cent respectively. Atherton had the lowest rate at 44.3 per cent, followed by Cheetham Hill at 44.7 per cent. Atif Iqbal, owner of Astra Driving School, said “Learners give themselves the best chance by practising on the kind of roads used around their test centre and taking a mock test before the real one.”
candidates.source_title: Rochdale and Bury record biggest driving test pass rate increases in Greater Manchester
